This kit is designed for simple on/off remote control, not high-speed continuous data transmission. To avoid interference, limit transmissions to a few commands per second . GENERAL DESCRIPTION The ADuM1201 are dual-channel digital isolators based on the Analog Devices, Inc., iCoupler® technology. Combining high speed CMOS and monolithic transformer technologies, these isolation components provide outstanding performance characteristics superior to alternatives, such as optocouplers. By avoiding the use of LEDs and photodiodes, iCoupler devices remove the design difficulties commonly associated with optocouplers.

The typical optocoupler concerns regarding uncertain current transfer ratios, nonlinear transfer functions, and temperature and lifetime effects are eliminated with the simple iCoupler digital interfaces and stable performance characteristics. The need for external drivers and other discrete components is eliminated with these iCoupler products. Furthermore, iCoupler devices consume one-tenth to one-sixth the power of optocouplers at comparable signal data rates.

A quartz crystal provides both series and parallel resonance. The series resonance is a few kilohertz lower than the parallel one. Crystals below 30 MHz are generally operated between series and parallel resonance, which means that the crystal appears as an inductive reactance in operation, this inductance forming a parallel resonant circuit with externally connected parallel capacitance. Any small additional capacitance in parallel with the crystal will thus pull the frequency downwards. Moreover, the effective inductive reactance of the crystal can be reduced by adding a capacitor in series with the crystal. This latter technique can provide a useful method of trimming the oscillatory frequency within a narrow range; in this case inserting a capacitor in series with the crystal will raise the frequency of oscillation. For a crystal to operate at its specified frequency, the electronic circuit has to be exactly that specified by the crystal manufacturer. Note that these points imply a subtlety concerning crystal oscillators in this frequency range: the crystal does not usually oscillate at precisely either of its resonant frequencies.

Crystals above 30 MHz (up to >200 MHz) are generally operated at series resonance where the impedance appears at its minimum and equal to the series resistance. For these crystals the series resistance is specified (<100 Ω) instead of the parallel capacitance. To reach higher frequencies, a crystal can be made to vibrate at one of its overtone modes, which occur near multiples of the fundamental resonant frequency. Only odd numbered overtones are used. Such a crystal is referred to as a 3rd, 5th, or even 7th overtone crystal. To accomplish this, the oscillator circuit usually includes additional LC circuits to select the desired overtone.

The Arduino Uno is a microcontroller board based on the ATmega328. Arduino is an open-source, prototyping platform and its simplicity makes it ideal for hobbyists to use as well as professionals. The Arduino Uno has 14 digital input/output pins (of which 6 can be used as PWM outputs), 6 analog inputs, a 16 MHz crystal oscillator, a USB connection, a power jack, an ICSP header, and a reset button. It contains everything needed to support the microcontroller; simply connect it to a computer with a USB cable or power it with a AC-to-DC adapter or battery to get started.

"Uno" means one in Italian and is named to mark the upcoming release of Arduino 1.0. The Arduino Uno and version 1.0 will be the reference versions of Arduno, moving forward. The Uno is the latest in a series of USB Arduino boards, and the reference model for the Arduino platform.

makers-451093.summary: UNI-T UT620C+ is a high-precision micro-ohmmeter designed for measuring low resistance in electrical components, ideal for industrial and power system testing.

blocks.text: The UNI-T UT620C+ Micro-ohmmeter is a high-precision, portable resistance meter designed to measure a wide range of resistance values, from micro-ohms to hundreds of kilo-ohms. Utilizing a four-wire (Kelvin) measurement method, it ensures accurate readings by minimizing the effects of lead and contact resistances. This makes it particularly suitable for applications requiring precise low-resistance measurements, such as testing transformer windings, motor coils, and grounding systems.

Key features of the UT620C+ include a resolution as fine as 1 μΩ and an accuracy of up to ±0.1% full scale. It supports a maximum test current of 1 A and offers eight distinct resistance ranges to accommodate various testing needs. The device is equipped with a large backlit LCD display for clear visibility in different lighting conditions and can store up to 500 measurement data sets for later analysis. Its USB Type-C interface allows for easy data transfer to a PC, facilitating further data management and reporting.

Designed with portability in mind, the UT620C+ is compact and lightweight, weighing approximately 480 g including its rechargeable 3.7 V, 3200 mAh lithium battery. It features an automatic power-off function to conserve battery life, activating after 15 minutes of inactivity. The device also includes safety features such as input protection up to 36 V AC/DC and an IP54 rating for dust and splash resistance, ensuring durability in various working environments.

The UT620C+ is widely used in fields like telecommunications, power distribution, new energy vehicles, petrochemicals, and industrial plant grounding systems. Its combination of precision, versatility, and user-friendly design makes it an essential tool for professionals requiring accurate low-resistance measurements in both laboratory and field settings.

blocks.text: D8257C-5 200ns 8-bit Programmable DMA Controller IC 5V 120mA DIP-40

The µPD8257 is a programmable four-channel direct memory access controller designed to transfer data between peripheral devices and memory without heavy CPU involvement. It is built for 8080A/8085A-based systems and can move data efficiently by taking control of the bus when a peripheral requests service. This makes it useful where fast block transfers and reduced processor overhead are important.

When a DMA request arrives, the controller generates the proper memory address sequence, selects the correct channel, and handles the data transfer timing automatically. It supports both input and output data movement, so it can read from memory to a peripheral or write from a peripheral into memory. The device also provides control signals that keep the transfer synchronized with the system.

The µPD8257 also supports DMA read, DMA write, and DMA verify operations, along with terminal count and priority handling for multiple channels. Its role is to simplify data movement in microprocessor systems by managing repetitive transfer tasks in hardware, allowing the CPU to continue other work while the controller handles the transfer cycle.

makers-489593.summary: A 24.000MHz fundamental frequency quartz crystal in a standard HC-49/U through-hole package, providing a precise and stable clock signal for digital circuits.

blocks.text: The HC49/U is a through-hole quartz crystal resonator housed in a standard HC-49/U package. This package is a classic, leaded metal casing that provides robustness and stability for the enclosed quartz crystal blank. The component is designed for wave soldering onto printed circuit boards and is not moisture sensitive, which simplifies storage and handling processes. Its construction involves resistance welding, ensuring a reliable and hermetic seal to protect the sensitive internal element from environmental factors.

This specific component is calibrated to a fundamental frequency of 24.000 MHz. Operating at its fundamental frequency means that the crystal’s oscillation is based on its primary, natural mechanical resonance. This is in contrast to overtone modes, which are higher harmonics of the fundamental frequency. The fundamental mode operation is typically chosen for frequencies up to approximately 24 MHz, making this crystal a standard choice for clock generation in many digital circuits within this frequency range.

The crystal’s primary function is to generate a highly precise and stable clock signal. Its performance is characterized by key parameters such as frequency tolerance and stability over a specified temperature range. makers-337166.summary: UNI-T UT07B-EU is a plug-in socket tester for 230 V EU outlets; it detects wiring faults and tests RCD (≈30 mA), with LED status indicators and compact form.

blocks.text: The UNI-T UT07B-EU socket tester is a compact plug-in device designed to check wiring correctness in AC mains outlets. You insert it into a standard European socket, and its LED indicators light up in various combinations to show whether the live (L), neutral (N), and earth (E/PE) connections are correct, reversed, or missing. It makes wiring verification fast and intuitive by eliminating guesswork.

Beyond basic wiring checks, the UT07B-EU includes an RCD (residual current device) test function, allowing users to press a button that induces a small leakage current (approx. 30 mA) to verify whether a protective device (RCD) will trip under fault conditions. This extends its usefulness from mere wiring diagnostics to safety verification of protective devices. The housing is molded from durable plastic and sized to be portable, with LED status lights clearly visible on its face.

In use, this tester becomes a go-to tool for electricians, installers, safety inspectors, and DIYers who want a quick, non-intrusive sanity check of socket wiring. It helps detect common wiring faults missing earth, reversed live/neutral, absent neutral, or incorrect phase orientation before connecting sensitive or critical equipment. Because of its simplicity, it’s also useful for preliminary safety checks in homes or sites without needing to bring out a full multimeter or tester kit.
LED indication of wiring status (various lamp combinations).

makers-523.summary: L293 Motor Driver Shield allows to control 4 DC motors or 2 stepper motors using Arduino kits. With adjustable direction and speed of rotation.

blocks.text: The module allows you to control four DC motors (DC) or two stepper motors using Arduino kits. The system allows to adjust the direction and speed of rotation of the motors with a current consumption of up to 600 mA.
Drive 4 DC motors with speed and direction control
The L293D Motor Shield can drive up to 4 DC motors at voltages from 4.5 – 25V and at currents of up to 1.2A peak (600mA continuous) per motor with speed and direction control.
The module can also support up to 2 stepper motors. Each stepper motor takes the place of 2 of the DC motors, so you can run 2 stepper motors or 1 stepper motor and 2 DC motors or 4 DC motors.

The shield also technically supports 2 servo motors for which there are two 3-pin headers on the module. Unfortunately, it powers the servo motors directly off the Arduino 5V which is usually not a great idea. Doing so can overheat the Arduino on-board 5V regulator as well as induce electrical noise into the Arduino 5V power causing intermittent problems that are difficult to troubleshoot.

On the plus side, it does have a 100uF capacitor on these power pins which does help somewhat. If using this feature, use only with small servos like the SG90, and keep an eye out for any issues. As another option, the traces to the 5V center pins on the servo headers can be easily cut and rewired to a separate 5V power source or the motor source if powered off of 5-6V.
Motor voltage must be between 4.5 – 25V. This power can be shared with the Arduino or be separate. To select this, there is a jumper near the 2 terminal power connector labeled PWR.
When this jumper is installed, the power from the Arduino DC power jack is also connected to the motors. Vin (marked 9V on the board) is brought up from the Arduino to power the motors.

When the jumper is removed, that isolates the motor power from the Arduino and it must be supplied separately by connecting power to the 2 terminal power connector. Note: Do not apply power to the 2 terminal power connector with the jumper in place or it will short the two power supplies together!
+M = Motor Vcc which must be between 4.5 and 25V.
The motor connections are via two screw terminals for each motor and are labeled M1 through M4. The center terminal on the 5-pos terminal blocks are connected to ground.

The wiring of which lead of the motor connects to which terminal is somewhat arbitrary and relative to what you consider forward vs reverse motor operation. If the motor goes in the opposite direction that you expect, simply reverse the wiring.

Stepper motors are typically 4 wires. Coil 1 will connect across one motor port such as M1 (M3) and coil 2 will connect across the other motor port such as M2 (M4). If the stepper motor has 5 wires, the center tap wire will be connected to the center ground terminal.
The shield has a remote reset button located on it for easy access.
The shield uses Pins D3,D4, D5, D6, D7, D8, D11 and D12 for DC and stepper motor control.
D9 and D10 come out to the Servo headers. D10 is connected to Servo 1. D9 is connected to Servo 2,

The other pins are available including the 6 analog pins that can also be used as digital I/O. These have solder pads so that a header can be added if desired for easy connections. Next to that is a row of 5V and Ground connections that can also be populated with headers and can be handy for hooking up various sensors.

blocks.text: This JoyStick Shield Module Robotics Control is an Uno compatible shield that allows you to turn an Arduino Uno or compatible into a game console or robotic controller. 3.3V to 5V Gamepad Joystick Shield Module Game Rocker Button Controller Expansion Board For Arduino Simulated Keyboard Mouse Module.

The shield sits on top of your Arduino and turns it into a simple controller. 7 momentary push buttons ( 4 big buttons + 2 small buttons + joystick select button ) and a two-axis thumb joystick gives your Arduino functionality on the level of old Nintendo controllers.

The X-Axis potentiometer of the joystick is connected to A0. The Y-Axis potentiometer is connected to A1. The analog inputs on a microcontroller read values over a range of 0-1023 (for typical 10-bit ADC inputs). The X-Axis and Y-Axis controls should read around 512 (midpoint) when the control is at rest. As the joystick is moved, one or both of the controls will register higher or lower values depending on how the control is being moved. The joystick also has a button ‘K’ which is activated by pressing the joystick down. This button is connected to D8.

There are a total of 6 buttons on the board (not including the one on the joystick) labeled A-F. The 4 large buttons are typically used for up/down/left/right or similar functions. The two smaller buttons are typically used for less commonly used functions such as ‘select’ or ‘start’ since they are less accessible / less likely to be pressed accidentally. All buttons have pull-up resistors and pull to ground when pressed.
The RX/TX lines are brought out to a separate 4-pin female header along with 3.3V and Ground. This can be used for connecting a 4-pin 3.3V Bluetooth device or a TTL serial device.

The I2C SDA and SCL lines are brought out to a separate 4-pin male header along with 5V and Ground. This is in addition to the normal A4/A5 location of these lines. This allows for easy attachment of I2C devices.
This connector allows a nRF24L01 RF transceiver module to be plugged in.
This female header connector is designed to mount the Nokia 5110 LCD that was originally designed for Nokia phones and provides a 48×84 pixel matrix.
This interface occupies the same D9-D13 pins as the nRF24L01, so you can’t use both at the same time.

This dual row yellow male header connector provides another point of access to all the buttons, joystick pots, 3.3V, 5V and Ground. The pin-out of this connector is labeled on the board to the left of the connector.

blocks.v: I1 and I2 · These are the input wires for the transformer, which is connected to the phase and neutral of AC mains
T1 and T3 · There are the output terminals of the Transformer, the voltage across it will be 24V AC
T2 · This is the center-tapped wire of the transformer; this wire can be combined with either T1 or T3 to get 12V AC across it. It’s very useful for rectifier circuits

blocks.text: Width 65mm without mounting tabs. 96mm with the tabs.
This is an AC transformer and the output is AC also.
If you need DC you need a power supply, not a transformer.

A centre-tapped transformer also known as a two-phase three-wire transformer is normally used for rectifier circuits. When a digital project has to work with AC mains a Transformer is used to step down the voltage (in our case, to 24V or 12V) and then convert it to DC by using a rectifier circuit. In a center-tapped transformer, the peak inverse voltage is twice as in a bridge rectifier hence this transformer is commonly used in full wave rectifier circuits.
How to use Center Tapped Transformer

The operation and theory behind a center-tapped transformer are very similar to a normal secondary transformer. A primary voltage will be induced in the primary coil (I1 and I3) and due to magnetic induction, the voltage will be transferred to the secondary coil. Here in the secondary coil of a centre-tapped transformer, there will be an additional wire (T2) which will be placed exactly at the center of the secondary coil, hence the voltage here will always be zero.

If we combine this zero potential wire (T2) with either T1 or T2, we will get a voltage of 12V AC. If this wire is ignored and voltage across T1 and T2 is considered then we will get a voltage of 24V AC. This feature is very useful for the function of a full wave rectifier.
Let us consider the voltage given by the first half of the secondary coil as Va and the voltage across the second half of the secondary coil as Vb as shown in the diagram below

When an appropriate voltage is applied to the LED terminal the electrons recombine with the electron holes within the device and release energy in the form of photons, this effect is known as electroluminescence. The energy bandgap between the semiconductor determines the colour of the LED

There are more and more hobbyists taking advantage of surface mount technology these days. With affordable tools like hot air and hotplate reflow ovens, electronics enthusiasts are shrinking their projects down to new levels of portability. Unfortunately, It’s not always easy to get your hands on small amounts of SMD parts so here’s a part that every project could use more of tiny little LEDs.

microohm-214891.summary: UTC 5N50 N-Channel Power MOSFET (500V, 5A) using DMOS planar stripe technology for efficient high-voltage switching—ideal for PFC, SMPS, and electronic ballast circuits. موسفت قدرة بقناة إن 500 فولت 5 أمبير مناسب لتطبيقات التبديل عالي الجهد مثل تصحيح معامل القدرة ومزودات الطاقة التبديلية والبالاست الإلكتروني، بتقنية دي موس لتحسين الكفاءة.

blocks.text: The UTC 5N50 is a 500V, 5A N-Channel power MOSFET from Unisonic Technologies (UTC), designed for efficient high-voltage switching in power electronics. Built using DMOS planar stripe technology, it delivers improved switching behavior and reduced conduction losses through a low on-state resistance design—making it a practical choice for modern high-efficiency converter stages.

A key strength of the UTC 5N50 is its ability to handle high-energy avalanche events, helping improve ruggedness in real-world circuits where voltage spikes and inductive switching can occur. This combination of efficiency and durability makes it suitable for demanding applications such as active power factor correction (PFC), switched-mode power supplies (SMPS), and electronic lamp ballasts, where stable performance and safe operation are essential.
In short, if you need a dependable 500V N-channel MOSFET for high-efficiency switching topologies, the UTC 5N50 is a widely used option in its class.
موسفت قدرة قناة إن 500 فولت 5 أمبير (UTC 5N50)

يو تي سي 5 إن 50 (UTC 5N50) هو موسفت قدرة بقناة إن يتحمل 500 فولت ويصل تيار المصرف إلى 5 أمبير، من تصنيع يوني سونيك تكنولوجيز. تم تصميمه ليقدم تبديلًا عالي الكفاءة في دوائر إلكترونيات القدرة، ويعتمد على تقنية دي موس مع تصميم الشرائح المستوية لتحسين أداء التبديل وتقليل الفقد أثناء التوصيل عبر مقاومة توصيل منخفضة.

يمتاز هذا الموسفت بقدرة جيدة على تحمل نبضات طاقة عالية في وضع الانهيار، وهو ما يزيد من متانته في التطبيقات العملية التي قد تتعرض لنبضات جهد مفاجئة أو أحمال حثية. لذلك يُعد مناسبًا لدوائر مثل تصحيح معامل القدرة النشط، ومزودات الطاقة التبديلية، ودوائر تشغيل لمبات الفلورسنت أو البالاست الإلكتروني، حيث تكون الكفاءة والاعتمادية عنصرين أساسيين.

A common charge/discharge port keeps wiring simple, while a long balance harness makes assembly straightforward for repair benches and custom battery builds.

Is this BMS suitable for LiFePO₄?
No; thresholds here target Li-ion (NMC/NCA). Ask for a LiFePO₄-specific 7S board if needed.
Can I parallel two packs with this BMS?
Only if the packs are matched in voltage/state and protected with appropriate fusing and cabling. Passive balancing does not equalize parallel strings.
A 7S Li-ion CC/CV charger with 29.4 V maximum output and current appropriate for your cells and wiring.
What happens if I wire the taps out of order?
Protection ICs may latch off or be damaged. Always verify B1…B7 in sequence before connecting the header.
This style performs passive balancing primarily near charge termination; minor bleed may appear earlier depending on cell drift.

blocks.text: Arduino Portenta Cat.M1/NB IoT GNSS Shield — Cellular + GNSS, Nano-SIM, u.FL

Bring low-power cellular and precise positioning to your projects with the Arduino Portenta Cat.M1/NB IoT GNSS Shield. blocks.text: ASP USB Programmer for AVR Microcontrollers
The ASP USB Programmer, also known as USBasp, is a compact, open-source programmer designed for AVR family microcontrollers.
It allows direct programming through USB without the need for a serial or parallel port, making it ideal for modern computers and embedded development setups.
It supports In-System Programming (ISP) via a 10-pin or 6-pin header, and is widely compatible with Arduino IDE, AVRDude, and other development environments.
Thanks to its onboard microcontroller, USBasp provides stable communication and reliable programming performance without the need for extra drivers on most systems.

Encapsulated in a robust DO‑35 axial glass package, this Zener diode is perfect for high-voltage reference circuits, power supply protection, and voltage clamping in industrial and communication electronics. The Zener Diode 36V 0.5W combines tight tolerance, low leakage, and reliable thermal stability needed for demanding designs.

The Zener Diode 36V 0.5W belongs to the BZX55C series. It holds its reverse breakdown at exactly 36 V with ±5% accuracy, making it ideal for reference-voltage generation, crowbar circuits, surge suppression, and high-voltage switch protection. Its rating of 0.5 W ensures moderate power dissipation, while its DO‑35 form factor offers easy integration into discrete or protoboard applications.
Key Features and Benefits of Zener Diode 36V 0.5W
The nominal 36 V Zener voltage, with a tolerance of ±5%, allows the Zener Diode 36V 0.5W to act as a stable voltage clamp—perfect for analog circuitry and sensor supply references.

With a 500 mW dissipation rating, this diode offers protection against small to moderate voltage surges and is suitable for use in shunt regulator topologies, pilot circuits, and amplifier bias stabilization.
Featuring reverse leakage below 5 µA at 30 V, the Zener Diode 36V 0.5W reduces undesired current flow that can degrade battery life or introduce noise in precision systems.
With Zzt around 30 Ω, it ensures tighter voltage regulation compared to high-impedance options, especially under dynamic load.
The glass axial package is rated for reliable operation across −55 °C to +150 °C, suitable for extreme environments. The black band indicates cathode, preventing assembly errors.
